replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
That's one of the issues with gen AI that a lot of people like to be ignorant of.

When anyone can one shot games the only people making money from that will be the people selling the services that enable it not the people making the games.

It's like the old saying, in a gold rush the ones making money and benefiting are the ones selling the shovels.

People will not care about anyone's AI generated game because they can just make their own version tailored to how they want it.

Pure AI gen games will become like disposable entertainment. You will be able to just constantly generate a new game every time you get bored of the current one.

That's why anyone using AI for game dev right now should really learn some actual skills in art and game design because if you're relying almost completely on AI then at some point you're going to be irrelevant.

replies.author: solidwhetstone
replies.body:
I do want to point out two things:

1. "Taste" is a thing. Whether you build a game with AI or not, there's no accounting for taste as they say- an AI can't taste something. Best it can do is go off of what it believes humans will thing tastes good. In many cases it can be right- but when it comes to something with coherent narrative, deep meaningful choices, etc. that's when you need humans.  
2. What has been commoditized is *execution*, not workflow. If you build a piece of AI software that visualizes something, cool- anyone can do that. If you build a tool with a specific workflow that solves an unmet need, you'll have something. AI is like a giant bulldozer. Sure one person can move a whole lot more stuff around, but you still have to have a plan for what you're even doing, otherwise you're just randomly pushing things around.

replies.author: fatheadlifter
replies.body:
I think taste can be taught.  Just because it's difficult to transfer that knowledge to a synthetic brain doesn't mean it's impossible.  Taste and judgement will at some point absolutely be transferred.

I'm an artist who has taste.  I make design decisions that are aesthetically pleasing to the eye.  Aesthetics is many things but it is a learned behavior, it's a skill.  A difficult one, one of mastery, but quantifiable at the end of the day.  Every decision that goes into aesthetics comes from somewhere, even the stuff that "feels right" or is intuitive has a source.  So I don't think we have too long before computers do this too and they do it really well, basically so good that I won't want to bother applying my skill anymore.

replies.author: cyberdork

> You will be able to just constantly generate a new game every time you get bored of the current one.
   
The implications are much worse.  
ALL media will be disposable. All movies, TV shows, music.   
  
In the end it will not even be based on a simple one-shot prompt. Your AI assistant will know not only from your past consumption, but also from you current biometrics what you like the most and what you will respond to the best at that very moment. So all media you consume will be generated based on your current state of mind and adapt to how you respond. Basically creating media Heroin. Every movie you watch you'll be like: 'Holy shit, this is the best movie I have ever seen.' Nobody will consume the same media anymore, everyone will have their perfectly personalized media. And why stop at entertainment? The same will happen to news consumption.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
I don't think people with talent and skills will ever become irrelevant. I think most human made end products will just become worth more than the average person wants to spend as AI will essentially industrialise media production. Chefs didn't become irrelevant when fast food outlets took over. Most people are just happy to eat crappy low cost food. There's always going to be a market for people that want something that wasn't completely generated by AI.

AI hasn't been around that long and I'm already numb to anything I know is AI generated with minimum effort no matter how good the output is. There's something that gives you a greater appreciation for a thing when you know someone with talent and skill has created it. When things get automated there's always a niche for people to continue making things mostly by hand.

From a game dev pov if you're not aiming to fit into that niche in the future you will be replaced by automation and you're not going to be making any money from generating AI games either.
